Inyoung · Listen & Shadow 01

First Class — hello, your lab meetings, your English so far, what you want
D O   E N G L I S H   W I T H   B R I A N
PART 1 · HELLO
👤 Brian
What are you researching right now?
요즘 무슨 연구를 하고 있어요?
research — 연구하다
💬 Inyoung
I'm working on something in neuroscience.
저는 신경과학 쪽을 연구하고 있어요.
work on ~ — ~를 연구하다 · neuroscience — 신경과학
같은 패턴으로 — I'm working on something in cell biology. · She's working on a protein assay.
💬 Inyoung
I'm at Korea University, but my lab is at KIST.
고려대 소속인데, 실험실은 키스트에 있어요.
lab — 실험실
같은 패턴으로 — I'm registered at the university, but I work off campus. · My department is here, but my desk is there.
💬 Inyoung
I'm in the second semester of my first year.
석사 1년 2학기차예요.
semester — 학기
같은 패턴으로 — I'm in my final semester. · He's in his third year.
💬 Inyoung
Most of my week is experiments.
한 주의 대부분은 실험이에요.
most of ~ — ~의 대부분 · experiment — 실험
같은 패턴으로 — Most of my day is reading. · Most of the month is data analysis.
💬 Inyoung
Outside the lab, I listen to music — alternative and modern rock.
랩 밖에서는 음악을 들어요 — 얼터너티브랑 모던록이요.
outside ~ — ~ 밖에서는
같은 패턴으로 — Outside work, I run. · Outside the office, I cook.
PART 2 · YOUR LAB MEETINGS
👤 Brian
Walk me through a lab meeting — who talks, and for how long?
랩 미팅이 어떻게 돌아가요?
walk me through ~ — ~를 차근히 설명해주다
💬 Inyoung
We meet once a week.
저희는 매주 한 번 모여요.
once a week — 주 1회
같은 패턴으로 — We meet every Monday. · We meet twice a month.
💬 Inyoung
The presentations are in English.
발표는 영어로 진행돼요.
presentation — 발표
같은 패턴으로 — The meetings are in English. · The slides are in English, the talk is not.
💬 Inyoung
My turn comes around once a month.
제 차례는 한 달에 한 번 돌아와요.
one's turn — 차례 · come around — 돌아오다
같은 패턴으로 — My shift comes around every three weeks. · The deadline comes around fast.
💬 Inyoung
The hard part isn't the slides — it's the questions.
어려운 건 준비한 내용이 아니라 질문이에요.
the hard part — 어려운 부분
같은 패턴으로 — The hard part isn't the writing — it's the editing. · The hard part is the timing.
💬 Inyoung
When I don't understand, I usually ask them to repeat it.
못 알아들으면 보통 다시 여쭤봐요.
repeat — 다시 말하다
같은 패턴으로 — When I'm not sure, I ask for an example. · When I miss it, I check afterwards.
💬 Inyoung
I'd rather say nothing than say it wrong.
틀리게 말하느니 차라리 가만히 있어요.
I'd rather A than B — B하느니 A하겠다
같은 패턴으로 — I'd rather wait than guess. · I'd rather ask than assume.
PART 3 · YOUR ENGLISH SO FAR
👤 Brian
Where did the English you have come from?
지금 영어는 어디서 온 거예요?
come from ~ — ~에서 오다
💬 Inyoung
Most of it came from reading papers.
대부분 논문을 읽으면서 쌓였어요.
paper — 논문
같은 패턴으로 — Most of it came from watching lectures. · Most of it came from school.
💬 Inyoung
I know the words — I just can't get them out.
단어는 아는데 말로는 잘 안 나와요.
get out — 말로 꺼내다
같은 패턴으로 — I know the answer — I just can't say it fast. · I understand it, I just can't explain it.
💬 Inyoung
The hardest part is speaking in front of people.
제일 어려운 건 사람들 앞에서 말하는 거예요.
in front of ~ — ~ 앞에서
같은 패턴으로 — The hardest part is starting. · The hardest part is keeping it short.
💬 Inyoung
When I'm nervous, I end up reading from the script.
긴장하면 원고만 읽게 돼요.
end up ~ing — 결국 ~하게 되다 · script — 원고
같은 패턴으로 — When I'm tired, I end up skipping steps. · When it's rushed, I end up rereading.
💬 Inyoung
I avoid it when I'm not confident.
자신이 없을 땐 영어를 피하게 돼요.
avoid — 피하다 · confident — 자신 있는
같은 패턴으로 — I avoid it when the room is big. · I avoid speaking up in large meetings.
PART 4 · WHAT YOU WANT
👤 Brian
Six months from now, what do you want to be able to do?
6개월 뒤엔 뭘 할 수 있으면 좋겠어요?
be able to ~ — ~할 수 있다
💬 Inyoung
In six months, I want to present without a script.
6개월 뒤엔 원고 없이 발표하고 싶어요.
present — 발표하다
같은 패턴으로 — In six months, I want to lead a meeting. · In a year, I want to write it myself.
💬 Inyoung
I'd feel good if I could answer questions on the spot.
질문에 바로 답할 수 있으면 좋겠어요.
on the spot — 그 자리에서 바로
같은 패턴으로 — I'd feel good if I could keep up. · I'd feel good if I stopped freezing.
💬 Inyoung
Correct me when I say something wrong.
제가 틀리게 말할 때 바로 고쳐주세요.
correct — 고쳐주다
같은 패턴으로 — Correct me when I mispronounce it. · Stop me when I go off track.
💬 Inyoung
I'd rather you stop me than save it all for the end.
나중에 몰아서 말해주시는 것보다 그때그때가 좋아요.
save it for ~ — ~를 위해 미뤄두다
같은 패턴으로 — I'd rather hear it now than later. · I'd rather you push me than go easy.
